evidence_packet.lead: Cheshire East Council says some of the site needs to be returned to its original state
evidence_packet.summary: Cheshire East Council says some of the site needs to be returned to its original state
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The owner of land earmarked for a proposed data centre is facing action over failing to restore the site to its original state Land off Millington Road near Little Bollington, near Lymm, Cheshire, was used as a compound for vehicles working on upgrades to nearby motorways, and now forms part of a site on which a tech firm wants to build a large data centre compound Cheshire East Council said the enforcement action against the Tatton Estate was not linked to the data centre plan, but campaigners against the 60-acre facility hope the council action will make it more difficult for the proposals to get planning permission Tatton Estate said it was appealing against the enforcement notice Data centres are typically large warehouses that store servers that process and distribute information online The artificial intelligence boom has coincided with a significant increase in the number of proposals to build them but the plans near Little Bollington are facing some opposition from nearby residents

evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester's Metrolink tram network will still be subject to some minor route changes
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester's Metrolink tram network will still be subject to some minor route changes
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tram services are due to return to normal on Greater Manchester's Metrolink network on Monday after two weeks of major disruption Improvement works have taken place at Deansgate-Castlefield and Trafford Bar, as well as in Manchester city centre, meaning no services ran on three Metrolink lines over that time A spokesman for Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed the work was on schedule to have been completed However, passengers have been warned that some minor route changes through the city centre will remain in place until Wednesday, with travellers advised to check the TfGM website , external Vernon Everitt, Greater Manchester's transport commissioner, told BBC Radio Manchester 's Hot Seat programme the works would be "the last big closures for a while" "Unfortunately there's never a good time to do these closures and I do apologise, but everyone will reap the benefits of it."

evidence_packet.title: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket
evidence_packet.lead: Lewis Rimmer was in an induced coma after being hit by a car and suffering life-changing injuries
evidence_packet.summary: Lewis Rimmer was in an induced coma after being hit by a car and suffering life-changing injuries
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket - BBC News Image source, Sarah Rimmer Image caption, Sarah and Lewis Rimmer, pictured with their daughters, have vowed to stay positive By Lauren Hirst North West Published 1 November 2026 Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night. Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in the car park of a Sainsbury's store in Bolton, Greater Manchester - just moments after he bought a lottery ticket. The doting father was airlifted to the Royal Preston Hospital where his family were told he had just a 30% chance of pulling through. Lewis spent weeks on life support and had more than 40 hours of surgery, including the amputation of his left foot. "For three weeks, I couldn't hear his voice, tell him about the girls or ask him for advice," said Sarah, reflecting on how life had changed one year on. "The girls couldn't understand why we couldn't Facetime daddy." Image source, Sarah Rimmer Image caption, Lewis Rimmer had been with his wife and two daughters shortly before he was hit In the following three weeks, medics reduced the sedation and each day Sarah would hope to hear the words "settled overnight", indicating he had progressed and was comfortable. "The next six weeks brought a whole new battle," she said. "Waking up, piecing together what had happened, learning to eat and drink again and slowly seeing the tubes and machines disappear. As the countdown to 25 December begins, cities and towns across the region have set the date to switch on their Christmas lights, marking the start of the yuletide festivities. Below are confirmed details of when and where events are taking place locally. Merseyside Southport: The annual ceremony takes place on Saturday 7 November, with free entertainment outside The Grand and performances from Regally Royal Parties from 16:00 GMT. Huyton: The Christmas lights switch-on will take place in the village centre from 15:00 to 19:00 on Friday 13 November. Prescot: The Christmas lights switch-on will take place in the town centre from 15:00 until 19:00 on Saturday 14 November. Kirkby: The Christmas lights switch-on will take place in the town centre from 16:30 to 19:30 on Friday 20 November. Greater Manchester Manchester: There will not be an official Christmas lights switch-on in Manchester, but the lights will be turned on across the city on Friday 6 November. Bury: The Rock Shopping Centre is marking its 15th year with a new tradition - its first Christmas parade and lights switch-on, on Saturday 7 November. Festivities start from 16:00 where visitors are asked to meet for the parade. title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening

evidence_packet.title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening
evidence_packet.lead: The NHS says rates have improved, but that too many women are still not getting checked
evidence_packet.summary: The NHS says rates have improved, but that too many women are still not getting checked
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Over a quarter of eligible women in the North West are missing breast cancer screening appointments The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 50 and 53, then every three years after that until they are 71 Dr Paula Cowan, a GP and the regional medical director for primary care at NHS England in the North West, said "some people may be reluctant to come forward for a number of different reasons" but that "breast screening... detect cancer at an early stage" The NHS encourages women to continue to check their breasts regularly and to get any unusual changes to how they look and feel checked out by their GP Tell us which stories we should cover in the North West

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former football club chief executive has pleaded guilty to offences relating to the drugging and raping of a woman by her husband and others Karl Lindsay, 56, who resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged, has admitted the offences, which happened between 2015 and 2025 Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard Lindsay's offending related to the rape of the woman by her husband and others in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, and the administration of substances to stupefy her for the purpose of sexual acts The woman's husband, who is in his 60s and cannot be named to protect his wife's anonymity, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife, including rape The woman at the centre of the case was in court with one of her relatives and watched Lindsay intently as he entered his guilty pleas Three other men, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee, Scotland, Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport, and Graham Brougham, 74, from Northwich, have already admitted sexually abusing her at previous hearings

title: Len Johnson: Site revealed for Manchester boxing statue

evidence_packet.title: Len Johnson: Site revealed for Manchester boxing statue
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester could get its first Black city-centre statue after years of campaigning
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester could get its first Black city-centre statue after years of campaigning
evidence_packet.evidence_text: He was one of Britain's best boxers, but never became champion Born in Clayton, Manchester, in 1902, Len Johnson won more than 90 fights during his career but was barred from contesting the British title because of the colour of his skin He later channelled the fighting spirit he showed in the ring into campaigning against racism, becoming a trade unionist, civil rights activist and member of the Communist Party More than 50 years after his death, Johnson is set to become the first black person to be honoured with a statue in Manchester. But who was Len Johnson? Despite having little boxing knowledge or training, he got his first taste of the sport after a fight at work prompted his father, a former boxer, to take him to a local contest A few weeks later, after training by skipping with an old washing line, he stepped into the ring for his first bout at the Alhambra Theatre in Openshaw

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Warning: This article contains distressing content A man has been found guilty of murdering a head teacher who was dragged to his death for more than a mile while trapped under the wheels of a car Simon Richardson crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was cycling home from his job at Stretford Grammar School on the evening of 20 April in the village of Warburton in Trafford, Greater Manchester Prosecutors claimed Richardson, 35, fled the scene of the crash before stopping to try to dislodge the injured but still-living cyclist and then driving on with Mr Mullins still lodged underneath the vehicle Richardson was also convicted of dangerous driving and will return to Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court to be sentenced on Monday There were shouts of "Yes!" from the court's public gallery as the guilty murder verdict was announced

title: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket

evidence_packet.title: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket
evidence_packet.lead: Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in the car park
evidence_packet.summary: Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in the car park
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in the car park of a Sainsbury's store in Bolton, Greater Manchester - just moments after he bought a lottery ticket The doting father was airlifted to the Royal Preston Hospital where his family were told he had just a 30% chance of pulling through Lewis spent weeks on life support and had more than 40 hours of surgery, including the amputation of his left foot "For three weeks, I couldn't hear his voice, tell him about the girls or ask him for advice," said Sarah, reflecting on how life had changed one year on "The girls couldn't understand why we couldn't Facetime daddy."

evidence_packet.title: What does Wythenshawe mean to the people who know it best?
evidence_packet.lead: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing
evidence_packet.summary: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing
evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening

evidence_packet.title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening
evidence_packet.lead: Over a quarter of eligible women in the North West are missing breast cancer screening appointments The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before peop
evidence_packet.summary: Over a quarter of eligible women in the North West are missing breast cancer screening appointments The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before peop
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Over a quarter of eligible women in the North West are missing breast cancer screening appointments The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 50 and 53, then every three years after that until they are 71 Dr Paula Cowan, a GP and the regional medical director for primary care at NHS England in the North West, said "some people may be reluctant to come forward for a number of different reasons" but that "breast screening... detect cancer at an early stage" The NHS encourages women to continue to check their breasts regularly and to get any unusual changes to how they look and feel checked out by their GP Tell us which stories we should cover in the North West

evidence_packet.title: Ex-football chief admits offences linked to woman's drugging and rape by husband
evidence_packet.lead: A former football club chief executive has pleaded guilty to offences relating to the drugging and raping of a woman by her husband and others Karl Lindsay, 56, who resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged, has admitted the offences, w
evidence_packet.summary: A former football club chief executive has pleaded guilty to offences relating to the drugging and raping of a woman by her husband and others Karl Lindsay, 56, who resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged, has admitted the offences, w
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former football club chief executive has pleaded guilty to offences relating to the drugging and raping of a woman by her husband and others Karl Lindsay, 56, who resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged, has admitted the offences, which happened between 2015 and 2025 Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard Lindsay's offending related to the rape of the woman by her husband and others in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, and the administration of substances to stupefy her for the purpose of sexual acts The woman's husband, who is in his 60s and cannot be named to protect his wife's anonymity, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife, including rape The woman at the centre of the case was in court with one of her relatives and watched Lindsay intently as he entered his guilty pleas Three other men, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee, Scotland, Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport, and Graham Brougham, 74, from Northwich, have already admitted sexually abusing her at previous hearings

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Warning: This article contains distressing content A man has been found guilty of murdering a head teacher who was dragged to his death for more than a mile while trapped under the wheels of a car Simon Richardson crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was cycling home from his job at Stretford Grammar School on the evening of 20 April in the village of Warburton in Trafford, Greater Manchester Prosecutors claimed Richardson, 35, fled the scene of the crash before stopping to try to dislodge the injured but still-living cyclist and then driving on with Mr Mullins still lodged underneath the vehicle Richardson was also convicted of dangerous driving and will return to Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court to be sentenced on Monday There were shouts of "Yes!" from the court's public gallery as the guilty murder verdict was announced

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester's Bee Network has announced a series of changes that will be rolled out across its services The measures include free bus travel for 11 to 16-year-olds, rail integration and longer-term plans for daily fare caps The changes are expected to begin in the coming months and build on the franchising of the region's bus network, which was brought back under local control by former mayor Andy Burnham Here is a look at the plans set to affect passengers over the coming months Train stations across the region will begin joining Greater Manchester's Bee Network from December, with work continuing in phases until 2030 Under plans announced by Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM), the integration aims to improve rail services, reliability, infrastructure and the overall passenger experience

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The knife attacks that have rocked the Arndale SPECIAL REPORT: As Manchester prepares for the festive shopping rush under the shadow of three knife-related incidents in just 11 days, shoppers share their fears while police surge Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter , Eva Millett and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 05:56, 02 Nov 2026 As monsters perch on top of buildings and familiar wooden huts spring up across town , Manchester stands on the eve of its busiest shopping season. But Police stormed and surrounded the Manchester Arndale on three occasions in 11 days. It followed three knife-related incidents, which Greater Manchester Police does not believe to be linked to one another With the city's streets and shopping centres set to become ever busier as the weeks tick along before Christmas , some shoppers told the Manchester Evening News they feel 'nervous'. The incidents began with a 14-year-old boy stabbed on the ninth level of the multi-storey car park Witnesses reported seeing several people run from the shopping centre to the car park moments before the attack. Armed officers were soon in attendance on High Street, Withy Grove and Dantzic Street close to the Arndale, while shoppers' cars were kept inside a cordon for hours in Quick-thinking passers-by were praised by Greater Manchester Police for saving the young victim from life-threatening injuries. Two 14-year-old boys were arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and later released on bail

The strategic sites accelerator, launching today (Monday) will help stalled projects that are commercially viable and have str The scheme will help tackle barriers to development, such as planning issues, grid connections and access to finance, according to the Department for Business and Trade. Six to 10 nationally important developments will benefit through loans, equity and grant funding, as well as t These could range from science parks to defence, technology and manufacturing sites. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The knife attacks that have rocked the Arndale SPECIAL REPORT: As Manchester prepares for the festive shopping rush under the shadow of three knife-related incidents in just 11 days, shoppers share their fears while police surge Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter , Eva Millett and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 05:56, 02 Nov 2026 As monsters perch on top of buildings and familiar wooden huts spring up across town , Manchester stands on the eve of its busiest shopping season. But Police stormed and surrounded the Manchester Arndale on three occasions in 11 days. It followed three knife-related incidents, which Greater Manchester Police does not believe to be linked to one another With the city's streets and shopping centres set to become ever busier as the weeks tick along before Christmas , some shoppers told the Manchester Evening News they feel 'nervous'. The incidents began with a 14-year-old boy stabbed on the ninth level of the multi-storey car park Witnesses reported seeing several people run from the shopping centre to the car park moments before the attack. Armed officers were soon in attendance on High Street, Withy Grove and Dantzic Street close to the Arndale, while shoppers' cars were kept inside a cordon for hours in Quick-thinking passers-by were praised by Greater Manchester Police for saving the young victim from life-threatening injuries. Two 14-year-old boys were arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and later released on bail

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester weather Greater Manchester no longer in drought as Met Office issues Bonfire Night forecast After a week of heavy rain the north west is in 'receovery status' but it looks we're in for a dry week ahead Add to preferred sources News Damon Wi Mostly dry conditions are forecast for the week ahead, despite Greater Manchester no longer being in drought conditions, forecasters have said. High pressure is to bring mostly settled weather to the north west the Met Office say, which is good news for Bonfire Night After being in drought for much of the summer, all of north-west England, including Greater Manchester and Cumbria , was moved to recovery status on Wednesday, after England experienced its wettest week for two years, the Environment Agency (EA) said. But, severe drought remains Much of Wales also remains in drought after the UK's hottest summer since records began in 1884. At least 120% of average rainfall is needed over the next six months for the entire country to be out of drought by next spring, the EA said Tom Morgan, meteorologist at the Met Office, said: "High pressure will dominate, which is still unfortunately bad news for southern regions in particular, which are experiencing the severe drought conditions that we've seen for several months now. There may well be a few showers "But for all other parts of the UK, it's largely going to be dry."

It needed partnerships with private developers and talks with a Tory government But through it all Bill Moores stayed true to his roots. He became a key man in Labour's leadership as it got to grips with regeneration into the early 1990s He was deputy to Salford Council leader, Bill Hinds, when - thanks to the foresight of planning boss, councillor Ben Wallsworth - a shattered city showed signs of rising again Ben, previous council leader Les Hough, and then-chief executive Roger Rees, were the architects of a gamble. It was one that would transform the city and its reputation In an agreement finalised behind closed doors, the council decided to pay £1m for the city's desolate docklands, which had once been the spine of the city's economy. The strategic sites accelerator, launching today (Monday) will help stalled projects that are commercially viable and have str The scheme will help tackle barriers to development, such as planning issues, grid connections and access to finance, according to the Department for Business and Trade. Six to 10 nationally important developments will benefit through loans, equity and grant funding, as well as t These could range from science parks to defence, technology and manufacturing sites. And that's why today we are proudly supporting the Journalism Matters campaign It sees the news industry come together to celebrate the role journalism plays in underpinning our communities. When terror struck the Jewish community in Crumpsall on Yom Kippur in October 2025, our reporters were on the scene within minutes. Within an hour, we had confirmed tha As rumours spread, readers needed reliable information. We identified the victims, reported their tributes and followed every major development. In the following week alone, we produced more than two dozen multimedia pieces, including CCTV and exclusive audio But our reporting didn't stop there. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The knife attacks that have rocked the Arndale SPECIAL REPORT: As Manchester prepares for the festive shopping rush under the shadow of three knife-related incidents in just 11 days, shoppers share their fears while police surge Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter , Eva Millett and Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 05:56, 02 Nov 2026 As monsters perch on top of buildings and familiar wooden huts spring up across town , Manchester stands on the eve of its busiest shopping season. But Police stormed and surrounded the Manchester Arndale on three occasions in 11 days. It followed three knife-related incidents, which Greater Manchester Police does not believe to be linked to one another With the city's streets and shopping centres set to become ever busier as the weeks tick along before Christmas , some shoppers told the Manchester Evening News they feel 'nervous'. The incidents began with a 14-year-old boy stabbed on the ninth level of the multi-storey car park Witnesses reported seeing several people run from the shopping centre to the car park moments before the attack. Armed officers were soon in attendance on High Street, Withy Grove and Dantzic Street close to the Arndale, while shoppers' cars were kept inside a cordon for hours in Quick-thinking passers-by were praised by Greater Manchester Police for saving the young victim from life-threatening injuries. Two 14-year-old boys were arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm and later released on bail

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester weather Greater Manchester no longer in drought as Met Office issues Bonfire Night forecast After a week of heavy rain the north west is in 'receovery status' but it looks we're in for a dry week ahead Add to preferred sources News Damon Wi Mostly dry conditions are forecast for the week ahead, despite Greater Manchester no longer being in drought conditions, forecasters have said. High pressure is to bring mostly settled weather to the north west the Met Office say, which is good news for Bonfire Night After being in drought for much of the summer, all of north-west England, including Greater Manchester and Cumbria , was moved to recovery status on Wednesday, after England experienced its wettest week for two years, the Environment Agency (EA) said. But, severe drought remains Much of Wales also remains in drought after the UK's hottest summer since records began in 1884. At least 120% of average rainfall is needed over the next six months for the entire country to be out of drought by next spring, the EA said Tom Morgan, meteorologist at the Met Office, said: "High pressure will dominate, which is still unfortunately bad news for southern regions in particular, which are experiencing the severe drought conditions that we've seen for several months now. It needed partnerships with private developers and talks with a Tory government But through it all Bill Moores stayed true to his roots. He became a key man in Labour's leadership as it got to grips with regeneration into the early 1990s He was deputy to Salford Council leader, Bill Hinds, when - thanks to the foresight of planning boss, councillor Ben Wallsworth - a shattered city showed signs of rising again Ben, previous council leader Les Hough, and then-chief executive Roger Rees, were the architects of a gamble. It was one that would transform the city and its reputation In an agreement finalised behind closed doors, the council decided to pay £1m for the city's desolate docklands, which had once been the spine of the city's economy. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford's new £1.8m Chinese garden is a UK first Seeking quiet contemplation amidst half-term crowds, an M.E.N. writer steps into RHS Garden Bridgewater's new £1.8m Yangzhou Scholar's Garden. View 10 Images The Yangzhou Scholar's Garden at RHS Bridgew Add to preferred sources News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 08:05, 01 Nov 2026 It is an overcast mild October afternoon. There are no rays of autumn sunshine. But I am still optimisitic I am checking out a sanctuary next to a gently gurgling stream. Sadly any hope of quiet contemplation is shattered by a cacophony of children It is half term and Britain's fifth national garden is a natural destination for young families. A path to the new attraction at RHS Bridgewater in Worsley is the one I am taking It cost £1.8m and is meant to radiate peace and serenity. Twenty containers of authentic materials were shipped from China to create it. This included Fir timber used to make traditional hand-crafted mortise-and-tenon joinery and kiln-fired tiles and handmade brickwork from the s It is the Yangzhou Scholar's Garden and in old China they were found within city walls as the Ming dynasty was eclipsed by the Qing from 1644 to 1912. Designed by intellectuals, poets and retired government officials, as urban retreats, they were supposed to be a spiritual utopia

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital 'I lost all feeling from waist down': Man's devastating diagnosis after being sent home from A&E Paul King was diagnosed with stage four prostate cancer after months of unexplained back pain View 4 Images Paul King, 56, from Old Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 06:34, 01 Nov 2026 A Trafford man who was sent home from A&E with suspected sciatica before losing all feeling from the waist down just 12 hours later has spoken about how an earlier diagnosis co Paul King, from Old Trafford , had been experiencing "severe back pain" for months before a scan finally revealed he had cancer on his spine and lungs Devastatingly, he was given less than a year to live. The cancer had spread from his prostate to other parts of his body and pressing on his spinal cord, causing him to lose all feeling below his waist But more than three years on, the 56-year-old is living with stage four cancer that is being managed with treatment. Paul believes earlier access to diagnostic scanning could have made a huge difference to his outcome He is sharing his experience as the Manchester Evening News joins forces with The Christie Charity to launch a £42.5m appeal to build a new cancer scanning centre at the Manchester cancer hospital

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester has diagnosed the most lung cancers in the country as part of Lung Cancer Screening, as the NHS encourages more people to take up their lung health check when they get their invite The city is one of the first areas in England to roll out NHS lung cancer screening across all 10 of its localities, achieving the national target four years ahead of schedule New figures released at the start of Lung Cancer Awareness Month in November reveal that 1,829 lung cancers have now been diagnosed through the NHS Lung Cancer Screening Programme in Greater Manchester, with more than 80% detected at an earlier stage, giving people more treatment The targeted programme invites people registered with a GP in Greater Manchester who are aged 55 to 74 and who currently smoke or have smoked in the past for a lung health check on a mobile clinic which tours the city. Those identified as high risk are then offered a low-dose CT More than 208,738 lung health checks have now been carried out in Greater Manchester with 95,001 people going on to be referred for low dose CT Most of these people get reassurance that everything is OK but if anything is detected people are offered follow up tests or treatment

title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening

evidence_packet.title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening
evidence_packet.lead: The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 5
evidence_packet.summary: The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 5
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 50 and 53, then every three years after that until they are 71 Dr Paula Cowan, a GP and the regional medical director for primary care at NHS England in the North West, said "some people may be reluctant to come forward for a number of different reasons" but that "breast screening... detect cancer at an early stage" The NHS encourages women to continue to check their breasts regularly and to get any unusual changes to how they look and feel checked out by their GP

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Karl Lindsay, 56, who resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged, has admitted the offences, which happened between 2015 and 2025 Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard Lindsay's offending related to the rape of the woman by her husband and others in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, and the administration of substances to stupefy her for the purpose of sexual acts The woman's husband, who is in his 60s and cannot be named to protect his wife's anonymity, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife, including rape The woman at the centre of the case was in court with one of her relatives and watched Lindsay intently as he entered his guilty pleas Three other men, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee, Scotland, Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport, and Graham Brougham, 74, from Northwich, have already admitted sexually abusing her at previous hearings The trial of nine other defendants accused of sexual offences against the woman has been scheduled to start on Monday after a series of delays

A report was The Mayor notified the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government of the designation. The Secretary of State will, by Order, establish a Mayoral development corporation for the Area. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges In December 2023 a trial was launched to embed two Citizens Advice case workers in two Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) run hospitals in Manchester - the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital and North Manchester General Hospital This was further expanded in June 2024 to include Wythenshawe Hospital, and the MRI in March 2025, and St Mary's in December 2025 with funding through MFT’s charity, as well as a damp and mould focused case worker funded through Manchester City Council The team of six Citizens Advice caseworkers are aimed at providing better wrap around care for patients and addressing the link we know exists between poor health, economic hardship and housing issues The trial has been a huge success with more than 1,500 people supported across the trial locations With more up to 3m patients contacts across MFT each year this presented a huge opportunity to reach people who may otherwise have not known about the services provided by Citizens Advice, or the support they were eligible to claim

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

Written about the life and paintings of L. S. Lowry, it turned one of the region’s best-known artists into an unlikely pop culture ph Coming to Lowry this November, Matchstalks Remastered is a playful music-theatre performance inspired by the song, the artist and the city that connects them. Two performers, accompanied by live jazz musician Adam Fairhall and a record player, attempt to follow a constantly scrol As the record plays, movement, storytelling and slapstick collide. Kevin Egan and Michael Pinchbeck shift between performers, songwriters, Lowry himself and the familiar figures populating his paintings, using the structure of the original song to create a series of theatrical sc Along the way, the production follows Lowry’s footsteps around Manchester and plays with the way stories about artists are remembered and retold. How does a painting become a song? What happens when that song becomes theatre? And what gets lost, exaggerated or reinvented along th The performance also arrives in the year marking the 50th anniversary of Lowry’s death, offering an appropriately unconventional way to revisit an artist whose industrial landscapes remain closely tied to the identity of Greater Manchester

evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он приобрел большую и преданную аудиторию как в Турции, так и за ее пределами. 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне.
